key_insight: A language-agent system can autonomously calibrate a 112-qubit superconducting processor by turning expert know-how into reusable, auditable Skills.
engineering_relevance: This reduces calibration bottlenecks in large quantum hardware systems and points to a scalable, transferable workflow for future fault-tolerant processors.
method: Three-phase human-in-the-loop distillation of expert calibration knowledge
Fine-tuned an LLM on validated trajectories to orchestrate task execution
Implemented Skills as decision trees with measurement commands, acceptance criteria, and audit logs
evidence_signal: The system autonomously calibrated 108 of 112 qubits in 4.7 hours, with 4–5× speedup over manual full-device calibration and 14/16 agreement versus expert manual calibration on a subset.
watch_item: Low-level control still requires hardware-specific interface adaptation, so portability is strongest at the decision-logic level rather than the device API level.
paper_title: Vibe Calibration: Autonomous Bring-up of a 112-Qubit Superconducting Quantum Processor by a Skill-Orchestrating Language Agent
